definitions.type: real Euclidean vector space with measure
definitions.definition: V=R^n, realized as tuples (x_1,...,x_n). Its topology is the Euclidean topology and its measure dx is the product of n one-dimensional Lebesgue measures. Compactness, continuity and derivatives use these topologies; integrable means Lebesgue absolutely integrable.

W=R^m with inner product v·w=sum_{k=1}^m v_k w_k and norm |v|=(sum_{k=1}^m v_k^2)^(1/2). On V the same convention uses n coordinates. The squared norm and dot product in all formulas have this meaning.

u_t(x,r) is the derivative at r of the one-variable map ρ↦u(x,ρ). Derivatives are ordinary Fréchet derivatives in coordinate directions; outside their differentiability set use the total derivative convention zero. This convention grants no differentiability.

definitions.type: family indexed by j=1,...,n of functions V×(0,∞)→W
definitions.definition: u_j(x,r)=∂_{x_j}u(x,r), the coordinate derivative in the jth spatial direction.

definitions.type: family indexed by j=1,...,n of functions V×(0,∞)→W

definitions.definition: Δu(x,r)=sum_{j=1}^n u_jj(x,r), component by component. The gradient D_x u has columns u_j; its Frobenius square is sum_{j=1}^n |u_j|^2.

inputs.statement: u:R^n×(0,∞)→R^m is jointly smooth: every finite-order coordinate partial derivative exists and is continuous on this open domain.
For every x∈R^n and every r>0, |u(x,r)|=1.
For every x∈R^n and every r>0 there exists a real scalar a with u_tt(x,r)−Δu(x,r)=a u(x,r). No regularity or globally chosen scalar field is assumed.

For any nontrivially normed field 𝕜, normed ring Z with a normed 𝕜-algebra structure, maps φ,ψ:𝕜→Z, point z∈𝕜 and vectors φ',ψ'∈Z: if φ has derivative φ' at z and ψ has derivative ψ' at z, then their pointwise product has derivative φ' ψ(z)+φ(z) ψ' at z. Here having derivative is the usual first-order difference-quotient limit.

output.statement: For every x∈V and r>0, u(x,r)·u_t(x,r)=0 and u_t(x,r)·(u_tt(x,r)−Δu(x,r))=0. Moreover u(x,r)·u_tt(x,r)=−|u_t(x,r)|^2, and for every 1≤j≤n, u(x,r)·u_jj(x,r)=−|u_j(x,r)|^2. For every real a satisfying u_tt(x,r)−Δu(x,r)=a u(x,r), a=sum_{j=1}^n|u_j(x,r)|^2−|u_t(x,r)|^2; consequently u_tt−Δu=(sum_j|u_j|^2−|u_t|^2)u pointwise. No derivative of a is asserted or used.

binders.type: real scalar under the displayed normality condition

locals.declaration: Choose a from H005 at (x,r), so u_tt(x,r)−Δu(x,r)=a u(x,r).
For the spatial identities fix any spatial index j.

argument.text: Fix x∈V and r>0. H002 supplies continuous derivatives of every order near (x,r). H004 implies u·u=1. Apply M001 to the square of each real component of the time curve ρ↦u(x,ρ) and add the m derivatives. Differentiating this constant identity gives 2sum_{k=1}^m u_k (u_t)_k=2u·u_t=0, hence u·u_t=0. Since the time and point were arbitrary this identity holds on the entire open domain.

produces.statement: For every y∈V and ρ>0, u(y,ρ)·u_t(y,ρ)=0.

argument.text: Choose the pointwise scalar a using H005. Dot u_tt−Δu=a u with u_t. By F001 and symmetry of the real dot product, u_t·(u_tt−Δu)=a(u_t·u)=0. This uses only the value of a at the chosen point, with no differentiation or regularity of a.

Differentiate the identity in F001 in time, using M001 on each component product and H002 to supply both derivatives: |u_t|^2+u·u_tt=0. For a spatial index j, differentiating u·u=1 in x_j by M001 first gives u·u_j=0 at every point. Differentiate that identity once more in x_j, again by M001, to obtain |u_j|^2+u·u_jj=0. These finite component sums establish u·u_tt=−|u_t|^2 and u·u_jj=−|u_j|^2 for every j.

produces.statement: u(x,r)·u_tt(x,r)=−|u_t(x,r)|^2, and for every 1≤i≤n, u(x,r)·u_ii(x,r)=−|u_i(x,r)|^2, where u_i and u_ii are the i-indexed members of the globally defined families u_j and u_jj.

argument.text: Dot the chosen normality equation with u. H004 gives |u|^2=1; F003 and Δu=sum_j u_jj therefore give a=u·(u_tt−Δu)=sum_j|u_j|^2−|u_t|^2. The same calculation applies to any real scalar satisfying that equation, hence gives the claimed universally conditional scalar formula. Substituting it back gives the explicit wave-map equation. F001, F002 and F003 give all remaining clauses. Generalize over x and r; the existentially selected scalar does not escape.
